PETITIONER: Sri.Avinash B.,
 S/o. Babu M.,
 Aged about 32 years,
 R/o. Ward No.21,
 Gandhi Circle, Malur town,
 Kolar Dist.

(By Sri T.V.Ramesh, Advocate)
 -Vs- RESPONDENTS:1. M/s.AS Transports,
 No.2/59, Kalayan Mandaba Street,
 Vellalapalayam Pollachi,
 Coimbatore-642 120.
 Represented by its proprietor  Ajith Kumar P.
 (Absent)
 2.

The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.,
 Motor TP HUB, Mahalakshmi  Chambers, No.9, 2nd floor, M.G.Road,
 Bangalore-560 001.
(By Sri M.Muniraju, Advocate )

* **
 SCCH-1 2 MVC No.2702/2023  JUDGMENT Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation from the respondents who are the owner and insurer of Lorry bearing No.TN-41-AX-7992 alleging that on 10.02.2023 at about 7.10 p.m., on Malur-Hosakote road when Avinash B vs As Transports on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4940915/
1 riding motorcycle bearing No.KA-08-X-9507 in front of Al-Ameen college, the driver of Lorry bearing No.TN-41-AX-7992 drove the same negligently, dashed the same to rear part of the motorcycle, thereby caused the accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
2. Petitioner took treatment at Kempanna Hospital, Hosakote and Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru.
3. Regarding accident Hosakote traffic police registered a case in crime No.27/2023.
4. As on the date of accident petitioner being aged 32 years used to earn Rs.50,000/- p.m. by wholesale potato business.
5. Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 owner of the Lorry remained absent.

6. In response to the notice, the respondent No.2 Insurance Company appeared through his advocate and filed written statement denying the allegation regarding reason, mode of accident,
nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.
In para No.8 of the written statement, respondent No.2 asserted that petitioner contributed 50% negligence for the alleged accident.

7. On the basis of the pleadings on 02.02.2024, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 10.02.2023 at about 7.10 p.m., in front of Al- Ameen college, Hosakote - Malur road, Hosakote Town, Bengaluru district, he met with an accident and sustained injuries, was due to actionable negligence act on the part of the driver of the Lorry bearing registration No.TN- 41-AX-7992 as alleged?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order?
8. On 18.06.2024, 08.07.2024, 12.08.2024 petitioner deposed as P.W.1 and produced 14 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.14.
On 29.10.2024 petitioner produced evidence of Dr.Priyamvadha, Neurosurgeon as P.W.2 and get produced case sheet at Ex.P.15.

On 09.01.2025 respondent No.2- Insurance Company produced evidence of the Officer as R.W.1 and produced two documents at Exs.R.1 and R.2.
9.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the contesting parties and perused the records.

10. On the basis of material available in the file, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ...

Due to the negligent use of motorcycle bearing No.KA-08-X-9507 by the petitioner, due to the negligent use of Lorry bearing No.TN-41-AX-7992 by Manikandan at the ratio 50:50, accident taken place resulting in injuries to petitioner.

sentences.text: 2 Issue No.2 ...

Petitioner is entitle to Rs.1,78,330/-
with current and future interest at 6% p.a. from the respondents as compensation.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 11. Issue No.1:- In the evidence petitioner/P.W.1 stated that on 10.02.2023 at 7.10 p.m. when he was riding motorcycle bearing No.KA-08-X-9507 on Hosakote-Malur road, in front of Al-Ameena college, the driver of Lorry bearing No.TN-41-AX-7992 drove the same negligently, overtook the motorcycle from right side, suddenly came to the left side, stopped the lorry without providing signal or indicator light, thereby made the motorcycle to dash to the left side of the Lorry, thereby became the reason for the accident resulting in injuries to the petitioner.

12. In the written statement respondent No.2 Insurance company denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident and asserted that petitioner contributed 50% negligence for the alleged accident.

13. In the cross-examination, petitioner stated that, on the date of accident, he alone riding the motorcycle from Hosakote towards Malur and in the place of accident width of one side road is measuring 24 feet width.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that Lorry was running beside divider straightly.
Petitioner stated that Lorry was running on the middle of the road, there was a space measuring 10 feet between edge of the road and Lorry.
Petitioner stated that there was neither cross road, nor cross (left turn or right turn).
Petitioner admitted that as per MVA Report, motorcycle dashed to the right rear lamp of the Lorry.

Petitioner stated that before JMFC, Hosakote, he is defending charge sheet filed against him in C.C.No.1288/2023.
14.
In the evidence of P.W.2-Dr.Priyamvadha stated nothing regarding reason and mode of accident.

15. In the evidence affidavit R.W.1-Officer of the Insurance company an hearsay witness of the incident re- iterated the same facts as narrated in the written statement regarding reason and mode of accident.

16. In the cross-examination, R.W.1 admitted that after investigation, police have filed charge sheet against the driver of Eicher vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN-41-AZ-7992.
17.

Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR and complaint pertaining to crime No.27/2023 registered by Hosakote traffic police on 13.02.2023 against the driver of the Lorry bearing No.TN-41-AX-7992 regarding the accident taken place on 10.02.2023 at 8.00 p.m. between Lorry bearing No.TN-41-AX-7992 and Motorcycle bKA-08-X-9507 resulting in injuries to the petitioner for having committed the offence punishable under Section 279 and 337 of IPC, on the basis of complaint presented by M.Babu, S/o. Muniswamy.
Ex.P.2 is the spot mahazar dated 13.2.2023.
Ex.P.3 is the vehicle seizure mahazar dated 13.02.2023.

Ex.P.4 is the copy of sketch of place of incident in which Avinash B vs As Transports on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4940915/
3 it is noted that on the road in a semi curve area, accident taken place.
18.

Ex.P.5 is the motor vehicle accident report dated 14.02.2023 in which motor vehicle Inspector noted that when Inspector inspected the Lorry bearing No.TN-41-X- 7992, noticed scratch in the rear right side tail lamp and when verified motorcycle bearing No.KA-08-X-9507 noticed damages in the front body shape and indicator, handle bar at left side, left side brake lever dislocated and damages in the mirror and headlight.
Ex.P.6 is the copy of wound certificate in which reason for the injuries are noted as RTA near Nisarga Layout, Malur road at 7.15 p.m. while travelling in two wheeler hit to Lorry on 10.02.2023.

Ex.P.7 is the copy of charge sheet filed by Hosakote traffic police in Cr.No.27/2023 against Manikandan, S/o.Murugan, driver of the Lorry bearing No.TN-41-AX- 7992 and petitioner-Avinash, S/o.Babu, rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-08-X-9507 for having committed the offence punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC and Section 146, 196 of IMV Act (Petitioner used the motorcycle bearing No.KA-08-X-9507 without insurance coverage).
19.
In this case there are no reason to disbelieve the contents of police records especially sketch of the place of incident and IMV report regarding reason and mode of accident.

In this case there is no explanation on behalf of the petitioner for what reason in the accident rear right side tail lamp of the Lorry, front body shape and indicator, handle bar, left side brake lever and mirror of the motorcycle are damaged.

Hence, it is clear that on a semi curve area on Malur-Hosakote road, due to the negligent use of Lorry and motorcycle, collision taken place between the front part of Motorcycle and rear right side of the Lorry.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that, on 10.2.2023 at 7.10 p.m., at Hosakote-Malur road, in front of Al-Ameena college, within the limits of Hosakote police station due to negligent use of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-08-X-9507 by the petitioner and negligent use of Lorry bearing No.TN-41- AX-7992 by Manikandan at the ratio of 50 : 50, accident taken place between right rear part of the Lorry and front part of the motorcycle, resulting in injuries to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 accordingly.
20. Issue No.2:

In the evidence petitioner stated that in the accident he has suffered traumatic brain injury, bifrontal contusion, right front EDH extending across midline, left frontal acute subdural hemorrhage, comminuted fracture of frontal bone, laceration bone deep over center of frontal region of the scalp, laceration over upper lip, incisor teeth broken and dislocated, took treatment at Kempanna Nursing Home, Hosakote and Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru as inpatient from 11.02.2023 to 14.02.2023 by spending Rs.2,00,000/-.
Petitioner stated that as on the date of accident he used to earn Rs.50,000/- p.m. by vending vegetables and fruits.
21. In the written statement respondent No.2 denied the allegation regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.
22. In the cross-examination, petitioner denied the suggestion that in the incident, suffered simple injuries, never spent Rs.2,00,000/- for the treatment.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that as on the date of incident never earned Rs.50,000/- p.m.
Petitioner admitted that he has been treated without surgery.
23. In the evidence, P.W.2-Dr.Priyamvadha filed case sheet at Ex.P.15.

4 24.

sentences.text: In the evidence affidavit R.W.1-Officer of the Insurance company stated nothing regarding nature and consequence of injuries suffered in the accident.

25. Wound certificate, Discharge summary, medical bills, OPD record shows that in the incident petitioner suffered laceration over center of frontal region of the scalp, thickness over lower lip,
multiple laceration over upper lip, left central incisor teeth broken and dislocated, bifrontal contusion, right front EDH, left frontal acute subdural hemorrhage, comminuted fracture, took treatment at Kempanna Hospital, Hosakote and Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru as inpatient from 11.02.2023 to 14.02.2023 by totally spending approximately Rs.1,86,660/-.

entities.text: Kempanna Hospital, Hosakote and Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In the copy of driving license marked at Ex.P.11, date of birth of petitioner is noted as 29.11.1991.
Another document shows that petitioner having license of whole sale vending license at APMC market, Malur.
26. In the file there are no document regarding quantum of income of the petitioner.

Hence, I assess compensation under the head of pain and sufferings at Rs.60,000/-, under the head treatment charges at Rs.1,86,660/-, under the head of conveyance, attendant and nourishment charges at Rs.6,000/-, under the head of loss of income during treatment period at Rs.64,000/- (16,000/-x 4)
under the head of loss of amenities and future unhappiness at Rs.40,000/-.
27.

Hence, I assess total compensation at Rs.3,56,660/-.
28.

In view of the findings recorded on issue No.1, petitioner is entitle to receive [Rs.3,56,660/- -
Rs.1,78,330/-] Rs.1,78,330/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a. as compensation from the respondents.
Sl . No.

Heads of Compensation Amount Rs.
1) Pain and sufferings: 60,000.00 2) Treatment charges: 1,86,660.00 3) Conveyance, nourishment and 6,000.00 attendant charges:
4) Loss of income during treatment 64,000.00 period (Rs.16,000/- x 4):
5) Loss of amenities and future 40,000.00 unhappiness:
3,56,660.00
Less: 50 % negligence attributed by the 1,78,330.00 petitioner, rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-08-X-9507:

Total: Rs.1,78,330/-
Hence, I answer Issue No.2 accordingly.
29. Issue No.3: Copy of the policy marked at Ex.R.2 shows that as on the date of incident, Lorry bearing No.TN-41-AX-7992 had insurance coverage with respondent No.1.

In the file there are no evidence to show as on the date of accident, respondent No.1 owner of Lorry bearing Avinash B vs As Transports on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4940915/
5 No.TN-41-AX-7992 has violated any terms of the policy.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the owner and insurer of Lorry bearing No.TN-41-AX-7992 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer issue No.3 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.

The respondents No.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer of Lorry bearing No.TN-41-AX-7992 shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.1,78,330/- (Rupees One Lakh seventy eight thousand three hundred and thirty only) with current and future interest at 6% p.a., to the petitioner towards compensation.
The respondent No.2, being the Insurer of the Lorry bearing No.TN-41-AX-7992 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to his bank account directly.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.

(Dictated to the Stenographer-I, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 6th day of February, 2025)
(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.
